title: PersonalLLM: Tailoring LLMs to Individual Preferences

bias_targets.methodology: Calculating the representativeness score (based on Wasserstein distance) of simulated preference models' opinions compared to real human populations using the OpinionQA dataset for various political affiliations and ideologies (e.g., Democrat, Republican, Conservative, Liberal).
Comparing the opinion distribution of simulated user preference models to real human demographic groups (Asian, Black, Hispanic, White) using the OpinionQA dataset.

Measuring the opinion representativeness of simulated users against real human populations across various religious identities (e.g., Muslim, Roman Catholic, Protestant, Hindu, Atheist) using the OpinionQA dataset.
Evaluating opinion representativeness by comparing simulated models to human populations across different income brackets (e.g., Less than $30,000, $100,000 or more) using the OpinionQA dataset.
Assessing how well simulated user models represent the opinions of different age demographics (e.g., 18-29, 30-49, 50-64, 65+) using OpinionQA.
Calculating representativeness scores of simulated user models compared to Male and Female demographic groups based on survey responses from the OpinionQA dataset.
Comparing the simulated models' generated preferences to real populations stratified by educational attainment (e.g., Less than high school, College graduate) via the OpinionQA dataset.
Measuring the opinion distribution alignment of simulated users with real human populations separated by geographic regions (Northeast, Midwest, South, West) using the OpinionQA dataset.
